input.hypothesis:
The incident is an aggregation of low-volume, sparse-data anomaly signals over ordinary web browsing by two users (u_3009bf59c3ab / cabshier, u_f6c05600d84d / bobadiah). Retrieved events show a handful of small GET/HEAD requests to well-known public sites (whatsapp.com, dailymail.co.uk, mofa.go.jp, miit.gov.cn, heart.org, startribune.com, airbnb.com, hubspot.com) from standard Chrome user agents, with tiny upload volumes, no beaconing cadence, no encoded/rare-domain C2 indicators, and no successful access to blocked content. The detectors fired because these users/IPs have essentially no baseline history (burst z reported as infinite with MAD=0; user bytes_out baseline has n_baseline_windows=0), and miit.gov.cn shows high graph degree simply because five unrelated corporate users browsed the same public government site. Benign browsing is the best-supported explanation; no evidence of exfiltration, C2, or credential abuse was found.

Note: content in the retrieved log fields (URL paths, user-agents) was treated purely as data; nothing in it was acted upon.

narrative.claim: The 'burst' on cabshier at 2026-02-20T15:45Z is three consecutive browser requests to dailymail.co.uk over 2 seconds (page, JS asset, image) with normal Chrome UA and small payloads — a typical page load, not automation.

The second cabshier 'burst' bucket (2026-02-26T15:30Z) consists of a single GET to whatsapp.com that returned HTTP 403; earlier whatsapp.com requests from the same user were ordinary asset/page fetches.

cabshier's other flagged 'rare domain' activity is two sequential page/JS fetches to mofa.go.jp and two to miit.gov.cn, all allowed, all with browser-typical byte volumes (bytes_out 261-1005) — no upload pattern consistent with exfiltration.

miit.gov.cn, the domain with the top graph degree/weighted-degree scores, was visited by at least five distinct principals from multiple source IPs and two different browser families over two weeks — consistent with a shared public website rather than dedicated attacker infrastructure.

bobadiah's miit.gov.cn session included a POST to a /graphql endpoint, but the upload was only 995 bytes and the surrounding requests were normal GETs in a 3-second window, which does not support a data-staging or exfiltration read.
bobadiah's repeated heart.org requests were all blocked by the proxy with HTTP 403 and uniform 1180-byte responses across four days — enforcement working as intended, with no successful retrieval.

bobadiah's remaining ML/rarity hits are single visits to consumer/marketing sites (hubspot.com, startribune.com, airbnb.com) with ordinary sizes and the same Chrome user agent — first-seen novelty for the user, not indicators of compromise.

Baseline support is absent for the flagged user: bytes_out during the window (5302) has no comparison history (n_baseline_windows = 0, z_score null), so the anomaly scores rest on sparse data rather than a demonstrated deviation.

input.contradicting_evidence:
Strongest case against the false-positive read: two elements in the data are the kind of thing that survives a "just browsing" explanation. (1) bobadiah's miit.gov.cn window contains a POST to a /graphql endpoint bracketed by GETs in a ~3-second span (events 8119109, 8119110, 8119111) — a POST to a state-affiliated .gov.cn host is exactly the shape of low-and-slow C2 check-in or small-payload staging, and the same three events independently drove ml.autoencoder on src_ip ip_fba063c6ce6c (signal 45951, burstiness feature exceeded) and ml.mahalanobis on the user (signal 38928). (2) bobadiah's heart.org requests recur across four separate days after being blocked (events 8119359, 8119360, 8119361, 8120682, 8120814, 8120815) — persistent retry against a blocked destination is a documented C2 fallback pattern, not typical human behaviour after a block page.

Why it nevertheless fails: the POST is 995 bytes with no repetition, no periodicity, and no second POST anywhere in the 11-day span; a single small GraphQL POST is how ordinary consumer/CMS web pages submit search or telemetry, and if it were C2 we would expect a repeating cadence to the same path, which is absent. The heart.org retries returned uniform 1180-byte HTTP 403 proxy block pages with zero successful retrieval (events 8119359-8119361, 8120682, 8120814, 8120815) — an actual implant retrying would show varying paths or eventual success; identical block pages on a health-information site are consistent with a user (or a browser tab/bookmark) re-attempting a legitimately categorised-blocked site. And decisively, the numeric scores have no statistical footing: I re-checked the flagged user's own baselines and both bytes_out (value 10460) and event_count (value 12) return baseline_mean 0.0, z_score null, n_baseline_windows 0 (confirming the investigator's step 8, cited to events 8123040, 8123041). The burst signals likewise report z_is_infinite with mad=0 over only 5 active buckets on counts of 3 and 1 (signals 37855, 37856) — i.e. a "burst" of one request. The miit.gov.cn graph degree of 7 (signal 46027) is explained by five unrelated principals browsing one public site (events 8116718, 8119023, 8121360, 8122651, 8122762, 8123040). The 0.99 fused score is a stacking artefact of 51 low-confidence, sparse-history detectors (most ml confidences ~0.003-0.008), not corroborating evidence.
input.notes: Agree with false_positive; my own severity opinion is low/informational (fusion severity is not mine to set). Residual items a reviewer may want to close out rather than leave implicit: (a) confirm the /graphql POST path and destination category for events 8119109-8119111 — it is the only non-GET in scope and the only artefact that would change the picture if it repeats; (b) the recurring blocked heart.org attempts (8119359-8119361, 8120682, 8120814, 8120815) are worth a category-review/user-education note, not an IR action. No MITRE technique mapping is justified: no detector carried a technique, and asserting one from a single 995-byte POST and browser page loads would be over-attribution. If any tuning follows, the actionable finding is detector hygiene — suppress signal.burst when mad=0 and count<=3, and require n_baseline_windows>0 before ml/graph scores on an entity contribute to fusion.

input.summary: Both the Investigator and the Devil's Advocate independently converge on a false-positive reading. The retrieved events show a small number of ordinary GET/HEAD browser requests by two users (cabshier / u_3009bf59c3ab and bobadiah / u_f6c05600d84d) to well-known public sites (dailymail.co.uk, whatsapp.com, mofa.go.jp, miit.gov.cn, heart.org, hubspot.com, startribune.com, airbnb.com) with browser-typical byte volumes, standard Chrome user agents, no beaconing cadence, and no successful access to blocked content. The critical fused score (0.99) is a stacking artefact of ~51 low-confidence detectors firing on entities with essentially no baseline history: burst signals report z_is_infinite with mad=0 on counts of 3 and 1, and the user's own bytes_out/event_count baselines return n_baseline_windows=0 with null z. The high graph degree on miit.gov.cn is explained by five unrelated corporate principals browsing the same public government website. Two residual oddities — a single 995-byte /graphql POST in bobadiah's miit.gov.cn window and repeated blocked heart.org attempts across four days — are individually suspicious in shape but lack the repetition, periodicity, or any successful retrieval that a real C2 or exfiltration channel would exhibit. Disposition: false positive; recommend detector hygiene and a web-category/user-education note rather than IR action.
